summary.headline: CMS Info Systems FY26 revenue rose 3% to Rs.2,487 Crores; FY27 services guidance held at Rs.2,700-2,800 Crores despite a weak year.
summary.overview: FY26 was a reset year: SBI RFP delay, consumption weakness, offsite ATM market contraction and wage settlements together cost about Rs.150 Crores of services revenue, per management. Q4 services revenue recovered 6% QoQ to Rs.609 Crores and Q4 EBITDA margin improved about 280 bps, with EBIT margin at 19% versus 15% in Q3. Management retained its FY27 revenue goal and a 25% EBITDA margin aspiration, while declaring a Rs.168 Crores buyback at Rs.340 per share and completing two acquisitions (Securens closed, FSS signed and expected to close end-Q1 FY27). Management walked away from a Rs.700 Crores transaction-fee ATM contract, citing return thresholds.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.6% in Q4 FY25 and 15% in Q3 FY26
vs ~Rs.100 Crores in FY24 and FY25
vs ~1% of revenue in prior years

segments.name: Three platforms (new reporting)
segments.commentary: ATM management solutions 58%, retail and currency logistics 26%, technology and payment solutions 16% of FY26 revenue; FY22 split was 63:37 across the first two with tech at 7%. Management said segment-level profit split is no longer meaningful.

segments.name: Technology and payment solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs.370 Crores (16% mix), up from 12% last year; Hawkai revenue about Rs.200 Crores, doubled in two years. Securens integration takes live monitored sites to 50,000 against a targeted Rs.8,000 Crores TAM.

segments.name: Managed services
segments.commentary: Moved from number five to number three in MSP ranking. Customer mix shift: top-customer share fell from 58.42% in FY25 to 48.52% in FY26. Mid-size MSP receivable stress addressed via FSS deal, a secured loan and escrow arrangement.

guidance_outlook: FY27 services revenue goal maintained at Rs.2,700-2,800 Crores (17-21% growth on FY26).
FY27 total revenue goal Rs.2,800-2,900 Crores (13-17% growth).
EBITDA margin aspiration in the 25% range for FY27; management declined to firmly commit and said it will wait for Q1 results.
Q1 FY27 revenue run-rate target about Rs.650 Crores (implies about Rs.2,600 Crores annualised); HDFC contract expected to add Rs.50-75 Crores in FY27.
Medium term: services revenue CAGR of 13-14% over the next four years (FY30 horizon), against a 15% historical CAGR and 12% over the last four years.
Buyback: Rs.168 Crores (about 3% of equity) at Rs.340 per share, approved by board. Cash balance about Rs.650 Crores.
FSS acquisition expected to close at end of Q1 FY27; management would not yet say whether it is EPS-accretive in year one.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex Rs.350 Crores, up from about Rs.100 Crores in FY24 and FY25, with depreciation rising from Rs.54 Crores to Rs.59 Crores QoQ.
Route network cut by about 10% (Sept 2025 to Mar 2026) using ML-based optimisation.
Gig delivery model investment of about Rs.15 Crores to convert part of fixed cost network to variable and expand into tier 3 and 4 retail markets.
Securens acquisition closed and integrated; expected to be accretive in FY27. FSS deal signed in Q4 FY26, closing targeted end-Q1 FY27.
Algo MVS software going live in FY27 to enable value-added services on recyclers; ICICI recycler mix moved from 20% to 80% in two years.
demand_pricing: Order book: FY26 order wins about Rs.2,000 Crores, of which about 75% executed; Rs.400-500 Crores remains to be executed. All three large wins (SBI, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank) are fixed-fee, none transaction-linked.
Walked away from a Rs.700 Crores ATM contract at Rs.19 per transaction (about Rs.75 Crores annual revenue initially); management said the transaction fee model is effectively dead in ATM.
Market clearing transaction price for one recent bank RFP was close to Rs.25, versus interchange of Rs.19.

Pipeline of 6,000-7,000 ATM units across bank RFP stages in FY27, mostly product purchase plus services or fixed-price outsourcing; management expects banks to return to refresh cycles in FY27 but will update on pipeline at Q1 or Q2.

Pricing: CPI/WPI-linked contracts being expanded; annual price resets applied; off-cycle price increases sought for state minimum wage and fuel shocks. A peer price hike was reported the day before the call.
Q4 FY26 consumption and currency supply dipped in March and April; management flagged Rs.50-70 Crores revenue risk if weakness persists for 10-12 months.
Lower-yield retail and tail customers were exited; management may drop Rs.25-40 Crores of revenue in H2 to protect margin.

qa_highlights.question: What could cause FY27 revenue guidance to be missed, and how big is the gap to Rs.2,800 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.633 Crores Q4 annualised gives about Rs.2,500 Crores; HDFC adds Rs.50-75 Crores, reaching about Rs.2,600 Crores. The bottom end still needs about Rs.200 Crores from pipeline and new orders. Main downside is a consumption dip of Rs.50-70 Crores; no single large contract is assumed like SBI last year.

qa_highlights.question: Did a competitor take the Rs.700 Crores transaction-fee contract the company declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a competitor took it; management declined to name them. Management said Rs.19 per transaction is an attractive price for the bidder, but the company's return thresholds (25% margin, ROCE) were not met over the seven-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: How is ATM cash split for FY26 across ATM cash, retail cash and CIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give the split. It only said the 60:40 cash to MSP mix moved to 55:45, and that reporting now follows three platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Why would banks add offsite ATMs, and how do onsite and offsite economics differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks now treat ATMs as an alternate servicing channel; recyclers handle cash acceptance, video KYC and card issuance and replace branch transactions. Banks are increasingly funding capex themselves, which changes the economics for deployers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp for the SBI and ICICI contracts, and how should HDFC revenue be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: SBI runs 7-10 years, ICICI longer, HDFC about five years. Management suggested dividing total contract value evenly across years for simplicity, noting ramp, price changes and churn will vary.

qa_highlights.question: How do the FSS and Hawkai/Algo cross-sell and FSS transaction exposure look?
qa_highlights.answer: FSS contracts being transferred are the managed services ones; some carry transaction exposure, which management views as manageable given 2-4 years of history. Algo would be a new opportunity; Hawkai penetration among mid-size banks is low, and combined scale gives cost synergies. FSS is described as the highest-quality MSP business by management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from stressed MSP customers (28% of revenue) and the Rs.58 Crores of loans and advances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management converted unsecured receivables to secured loans for one MSP, took an escrow route on another and solved a third. Provision already taken in Q2 FY26. Management said there is no further risk expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the view on depreciation rising and on EBIT margin, and will the promoter tender in the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the depreciation rise reflects longer-term tech and capex investments, and that synergies from Securens and FSS may take a few quarters, while depreciation starts on day one. ROCE was about 25% in prior years. Rajiv Kaul said he will not participate in the buyback.

risks_watch: Consumption and currency supply: March-April dip; Rs.50-70 Crores revenue at risk if it persists for 10-12 months.
Fuel and wage inflation: fuel and vehicle costs about 6% of revenue; Q1 is seasonally lower-margin; the 25% EBITDA aspiration is not yet confirmed.
Revenue gap: about Rs.200 Crores still needed beyond the Rs.2,600 Crores run-rate to reach the bottom of the FY27 services goal.
FSS integration and closing at end-Q1 FY27; quality and network stabilisation take priority over pricing arbitrage.
MSP counterparty credit risk: mid-size MSPs under liquidity stress; recovery depends on escrow and secured structures.
Brinks-NCR merger could shift some MSP base over time; management sees it as a long-dated risk.
Depreciation step-up (Rs.54 Crores to Rs.59 Crores QoQ) ahead of revenue from new capex.
key_quotes: Setting in May, impossible to tell you today if we will hit it, achieve it or miss it.
I do not think there is significant risk as of today, but we would prefer to be conservative on this.
I do not intend to participate in the buyback at all.
Let us finish the deal in Q1, Baidik, and after that we can tell you better.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery, the M&A and the order book, but cautious on forward margins: management declined to commit to the 25% EBITDA aspiration and said it will wait for Q1 results. Evasive on specifics: it would not give the ATM cash / retail cash / CIT split, FSS EPS accretion timing, or the pipeline size, and deferred the depreciation question to the CFO.

adds.what: Gig delivery model investment (~Rs.15 Cr) to convert part of fixed cost network to variable and expand into tier 3 and 4 retail markets
Algo MVS software going live in FY27 to enable value-added services on recyclers

growth.why: FY27 total revenue goal of Rs.2,800-2,900 Cr (13-17% growth, midpoint ~15%) is held, backed partly by ~Rs.400-500 Cr unexecuted order book, HDFC contract adding Rs.50-75 Cr, and Securens/FSS acquisitions, but no new physical capacity is quantified and management avoided committing to the 25% EBITDA margin and flagged Rs.50-70 Cr and Rs.25-40 Cr revenue risks.
